audit_findings.title: The trend anchor may mix the current utility with the former midstream business
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical OE enters the 2016–2025 log-trend anchor; removing former midstream earnings, losses, distributions, taxes and disposal effects could change the fitted $478.2m anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: OGE Energy exited its former midstream business in 2022 as a result of selling all equity securities of Energy Transfer that were previously held by OGE Energy.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2022 exit is demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the 2016–2022 OE figures were restated to the current utility perimeter. The direction is not reliably inferable because removing earlier-period midstream results could change both the level and slope of the trend. With seven of ten trend observations potentially affected, the issue could matter, but its materiality cannot be established without the annual reconciliations.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each 2016–2022 OE build to filed utility and former-midstream results, remove all non-current-perimeter items and related taxes, then refit the log trend and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Non-cash construction allowances may remain in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 equity AFUDC $26.0m plus borrowed-funds AFUDC $15.8m; $41.8m combined, equal to 8.7% of the $478.2m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity AFUDC increases income and borrowed-funds AFUDC reduces interest expense while both are capitalized into CWIP; retaining either in equity-level OE can inflate the earnings base, with possible interaction with the capex deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Allowance for funds used during construction, a non-cash item, is reflected as an increase to Net Other Income and a reduction to Interest Expense in the statements of income and as an increase to Construction Work in Progress in the balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The non-cash allowances and their amounts are filed, but their omission from the OE reconciliation is not demonstrated by the supplied record. If both were retained without an offsetting treatment, the identified pre-tax exposure is large enough to materially alter intrinsic value, although the after-tax correction and capex interaction require a rerun.
audit_findings.action: Trace both AFUDC components through every annual OE build, confirm equity AFUDC is removed, reconcile borrowed-funds AFUDC to the retained-interest convention and capex line, and rerun the trend and scenarios if either component was counted.

audit_findings.title: Recurring removal cash could fall outside both earnings and the capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: filed removal cash of $93.9m in 2023, $70.3m in 2024 and $72.2m in 2025; the 2025 amount equals 15.1% of the $478.2m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Removal cash can bypass current earnings through accumulated depreciation and is separately reported from capital expenditures, so omission from both maintenance capex and a separate OE adjustment inflates annual OE and the trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: For assets that belong to a common plant account, the replaced plant is removed from plant balances, and the cost of such property net of any salvage proceeds is charged to Accumulated Depreciation.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash outflows are demonstrated, but the supplied valuation does not establish whether they were deducted elsewhere. If omitted, their scale relative to the anchor is plainly material and would lower value; if already included in maintenance capex, another deduction would double count them.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2023–2025 investing cash-flow removal lines to the corresponding OE capex deductions, determine the recurring maintenance portion, deduct it exactly once, and refit the trend and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may belong partly to future shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Future common issuance would increase diluted shares or allocate part of future incremental OE to new capital providers, reducing the OE per share attributable to current owners in the 5% and 8% growth cases.
audit_findings.evidence: Management expects that cash generated from operations, proceeds from the issuance of long- and short-term debt, proceeds from the settlement of the FSAs, sales of common stock to the public through public offerings and OGE Energy's Automatic Dividend Reinvestment and Stock Purchase Plan, or other offerings will be adequate over the next three years to meet anticipated cash needs and to fund future growth opportunities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings identify common issuance as a future financing source, but no issuance schedule, price or incremental OE attribution is supplied. This is a forward-looking financing risk rather than a demonstrated error in present shares. It should be monitored because a frozen denominator can overstate current-owner value if external equity is required to produce the modeled growth.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual financing schedule linking growth capex, operating cash, debt capacity, FSA proceeds, DRIP/public issuance and diluted shares; rerun base and bull cases on per-share OE, or document that modeled growth is financeable without additional common equity.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory cost deferrals may inflate the current earnings base
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 deferred depreciation and amortization $12.7m, equal to 2.7% of the $478.2m anchor; PISA regulatory asset increased from $22.9m at 2025 year-end to $64.5m at June 30, 2026, a $41.6m increase, while first-half 2026 deferred depreciation was $23.3m
audit_findings.mechanism: PISA/SB 998 deferrals suppress current depreciation and interest expense while creating a regulatory asset; OE is overstated if the associated investment is neither economically expensed nor deducted from cash available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: This legislation allows OG&E to establish a regulatory asset to defer 90 percent of depreciation expense and debt return associated with qualified plant investments, that are not classified as transmission or new generation, for recovery over an allowed 20-year period in a future rate filing.
audit_findings.explanation: The deferrals are demonstrated, but their treatment in the OE build is not. The 2025 depreciation amount alone is modest relative to the anchor, while the rapid 2026 regulatory-asset growth and unquantified interest deferral show that the continuing effect could be larger. The record therefore cannot establish total valuation materiality.
audit_findings.action: Trace annual PISA regulatory-asset additions, amortization and recoveries through net income, operating cash flow and the OE reconciliation; separately identify deferred depreciation and debt return, then rerun with each treated as an economic expense or required investment exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The FSA shares and their settlement cash are not represented on the same basis
audit_findings.magnitude: June 30, 2026 physical-settlement proceeds $191.8m, equal to about $0.90 per 213.334951m valuation share; adding them would raise bull value from $41.47 to about $42.37, still $4.55 or 9.7% below the $46.92 price
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation denominator includes physically issuable FSA shares, but the bridge omits the matching settlement proceeds, understating equity value per share on a physical-settlement basis.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, OGE Energy could have settled the FSAs with physical delivery of 4,613,372 shares of common stock to the counterparties in exchange for cash of $193.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is demonstrated. Its maximum directly computed physical-settlement correction is about $0.90 per valuation share, which does not change the conclusion even in the bull case because corrected value remains below market price. Alternative net-cash or net-share settlement must still be modeled consistently.
audit_findings.action: Update the June 30, 2026 bridge and denominator on one consistent basis: either include 4,613,372 shares and $191.8m proceeds for physical settlement, or exclude those shares and incorporate the filed $24.0m net-cash or approximately 514,000-share settlement obligation; rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2023 $51.6m, or 10.2% of filed D&A; FY2024 $70.2m, or 13.0% of filed D&A
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE, potentially increasing historical OE, the fitted anchor and scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $51.6m (10.2% of filed D&A); FY2024 $70.2m (13.0% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving unidentified D&A as an expense is conservative and is not an overstatement error. The residual amounts are large enough to matter if a meaningful recurring portion qualifies, but the record does not identify the components or establish that any amount is eligible for an add-back.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the filed D&A composition by asset and regulatory account for 2023–2024, classify economic depreciation, amortization and recoverable regulatory components, add back only amounts supported as non-economic and recurring, and then refit the trend and rerun all scenarios.
